classification.difficultyReason: Translate the window dimensions and graph into integration limits, integrate a cosine function and round the practical area.

content.prompt: An arch window 3 metres high and 2 metres wide is made in the shape of the curve $y=3\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)$. Find the area of the window in square metres, correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Unshaded cosine arch with filled endpoints, positive-direction axis arrows and the three supplied numerical labels. Ordinary graph marks are black.
spec.mathematics: The curve y=3 cos(pi x/2) on -1≤x≤1 has endpoints (-1,0), (1,0) and maximum (0,3).
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied graph information is visible; no integration or area answer appears.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
A&=\int_{-1}^{1}3\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)\,dx\\
A&=\left[\frac{6}{\pi}\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)\right]_{-1}^{1}\\
A&=\frac{6}{\pi}(1)-\frac{6}{\pi}(-1)\\
A&=\frac{12}{\pi}\\
A&\approx3.8\text{ m}^2\quad\text{(1 decimal place)}
\end{align*}$$
